cards.explanation: The answer is that David says No, they devise injustice in their hearts. He doesn't dance around it, friends. He says, "No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth." (Psalm 58:2) Both the hearts and the hands get named.

The answer is False. David says, "The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth." (Psalm 58:3) He puts the going astray at the very beginning, not later in life, friends. He's painting how deep this goes.

The answer is that the cobra shuts its ears. David says the cobra "shuts its ears, refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell." (Psalm 58:4-5) The charmer is skillful, and the cobra still refuses to hear. David sets that picture right beside the wicked's venom.

The answer is False. The prayer says, "O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions." (Psalm 58:6) David asks for the fangs to be torn out, friends. Nothing about lions lying down in peace.

The answer is True. David prays, "May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted." (Psalm 58:7) A blunted arrow is a dull one. He's asking for the wicked's weapons to be dulled.
The answer is that they never see the sun. David prays, "…may they never see the sun." (Psalm 58:8) This is a heavy part of the song, friends. He's asking God to end the wicked's reach.

The answer is that He will sweep them away. The psalm says, "Before your pots can feel the burning thorns—whether green or dry—He will sweep them away." (Psalm 58:9) It's fast, bakers. The sweeping comes before the pots even feel the thorns.

The answer is True. David says, "The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged…" (Psalm 58:10) The song goes from the wicked to the righteous here, friends. Their joy comes when they see they are avenged.

The answer is reward. Men will say, "There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!" (Psalm 58:11) After all the heavy lines before it, I think this verse lands on hope, friends. Reward is the very word the verse uses.

The answer is God. The people say, "There is surely a God who judges the earth!" (Psalm 58:11) David opened by asking if the rulers judge uprightly, bakers. He closes by pointing to the God who judges the earth.
